questions_used.question: Q1 — all 23 relations, or only the main paths?
questions_used.answer: All of them. Every relation once. I'd rather navigate a big canvas than lose a path.

questions_used.question: Q2 — one canvas with named diagrams, or several separate panes?
questions_used.answer: One canvas with everything, split into named diagrams I can read. Describe each one so I know what I'm looking at.

questions_used.question: Q3 — motion: does the source's slow, sparse dot request still apply?
questions_used.answer: Slow, sparse dots — one per live transition. Nothing on the historical ones, and no dot sitting on a border.

questions_used.question: Q4/Q5 — which C4 levels does the source support, and does it state any single container's internals (the brief's webapi example: auth, intake, jobs, persistence)?
questions_used.answer: Level 1 (context) and level 2 (containers) are fully supported. Level 3 is not: the source names no internals of any container — webapi appears only through its external relations (http in, reinstall/reprovision out, janitor proposals in, Slack out). The brief's own rule is 'include only if the source's facts support it', so level 3 is omitted rather than invented; level 4 (code/classes) the brief puts out of scope and the source has none.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: brief.md marks level 3 optional and forbids inventing internals; source.md states no container internals

questions_used.question: Q6 — may one C4 level take more than one diagram?
questions_used.answer: Yes, when the engine cannot hold the level whole: the frozen check reports 'above the readable budget (12/16)' for a one-diagram container view (probe-l2-one-diagram-tb, 17 nodes / 23 edges at 105x171 with 73 near-miss cells) and refuses to route it in lr ('no obstacle-safe route for wapi -> q'). Level 2 therefore ships as two container diagrams whose union covers all 23 relations, with the split stated per diagram.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: measured engine behaviour (probe-l2-one-diagram*, attempts-log.jsonl), and the skill's rule that layout may not thin content

questions_used.question: Q7 — is the machine-agent inside the system boundary or a machine-side actor?
questions_used.answer: Inside: the agent is how the manager observes its machines ('runs on host', 'register + heartbeat'), so context zoom shows the machine→manager heartbeat aggregate and the container level shows mch → agent → public gRPC → Postgres verbatim.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: source lists machine-agent as a component of the manager's own path list, not as a provider or actor

questions_used.question: Q8 — do the source's 'historical claims' need dashed (unconfirmed) edges?
questions_used.answer: No dashed edges: the qualifier is about the chat excerpt being evidence, not about any individual link being unconfirmed; no relation in the source is marked unconfirmed, so every edge is solid and the evidence status is recorded here instead of drawn as a style the source never states.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: source.md's 'historical' qualifier scopes the whole excerpt; the 'Fixed constraints' treat the 23 relations as the drawing's facts

questions_used.question: Q9 — does a context-level edge repeat each container-level relation, or expand into them?
questions_used.answer: Expands: one context edge per system-boundary interaction, with its expansion recorded in the coverage map (e.g. machine manager → machines 'boot+audit' expands to boot→mch 'boot.ipxe + S3 args' and ssh→mch 'run machine-audit'). No source relation is counted as dropped when its aggregate is drawn.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — reason: brief.md states C4 zoom semantics ('a context-level edge EXPANDS into several container-level edges … record that expansion, not a drop')

c4_capability_verdict.conclusion: The current skill + engine can carry a C4 ask at levels 1 and 2 only by (a) splitting one C4 level across several canvas diagrams because of the 12/16 readable budget, and (b) expressing C4 boundaries as hue families instead of boxes. The owner's canvas chrome (top divider, uniform divider width) is not expressible at all. A dedicated c4 skill would earn its place if it specified level-owned bands (a level heading over several diagrams), C4 boundary rendering, and the divider contract; today the visualize skill has no C4 vocabulary and the engine has no level concept.
